_why: ADR 0029's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py. This is
Jeske's finding -- she pointed at 'Y124C mutant' sitting in the
commentary of a row Terrium was treating as the enzyme -- so it is the
table whose correctness matters most to the people who gave feedback.
The ADR reports eleven mutations. This set carries the three that bear
on the SCIENCE rather than on plumbing: the negative-test inversion, the
unstated-reads-as-wild-type inversion, and the exact-tier filter that was
originally NOT CAUGHT. The remaining eight are wiring (forwarding a flag,
naming what was withheld) and are covered by the same suite; they are
listed in the ADR and are not re-derived here because each additional
mutation is another full pytest run and the set has to stay under the
per-call ceiling that killed the first run in ADR 0069.

mutations.description: is_wild_type becomes the negative test (status != variant)
mutations._note: The inversion the module exists to prevent: with the negative form every unlabelled row certifies itself wild-type, and `unstated` is the majority case in BRENDA.

mutations.description: the exact-match tier stops filtering variants
mutations._claimed: 0 failed originally -- the golden case only exercised the cross-species tier. test_exact_tier_excludes_variant_rows_from_selection closed it.
mutations._note: The finding worth keeping from ADR 0029. A filter no test can break is one somebody removes as dead code, and the day after that a mutant's constant is the enzyme's again.
